zh.question: 一只工蚁怎样感知附近线索，而一个没有总指挥的蚁群又怎样共同生活？
zh.observe: 先在 W1 的放大窗里区分触角、六足与大颚；再开始觅食，找出紫色踪迹第一次出现的位置。比较线索减弱和实体阻断，观察同一只 W1 怎样搜索。进入同一个巢，另用 L1 的发育记录观察卵、幼虫、蛹和成虫。

academic.title: 身体结构连接感觉与行动
academic.body: 触角是检测化学线索和接触的重要器官；三对足连接于中躯的胸部部分，大颚是口器。细腰、后腹部与外骨骼又承担不同作用。插图只为辨认这些结构，不是物种鉴定图谱。应把观察到的接触、转向和后续行为，与研究者对信息利用的解释分开。

academic.title: 踪迹与记忆参与局部选择
academic.body: 以黑毛蚁研究为参照，化学线索不是导航的唯一信息，路线经验也可能参与。这里固定个体与地点，让化学标记在返回者实际经过之后出现，并区分信号较弱与通路被阻挡。搜索、成功找回方向和绕行轨迹是有限教学例子，不是随机蚁群预测，也不保证全局最短路线。

academic.title: 个体发育与群体分工不是同一层次
academic.body: L1 的卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫属于另一个体的发育记录，不能把成年 W1 变回幼虫。工蚁参与照料、维护和觅食，蚁后主要繁殖而非逐只指挥。幼体需求、同伴接触和环境共同影响群体活动；任务、巢形、繁殖体系及信息素使用均有物种差异。

zh.misconception: 隐藏紫点只是隐藏解释图层，不会擦掉气味；蚁后不是总指挥，整齐的队伍也不等于万能的最短路算法。
zh.boundary: 四只巢外工蚁、一个照料工蚁及蚁后是有限教学角色。轨迹、招募延迟、记忆成功、信息素衰减和绕行结果均为作者选定；不模拟扩散、风、真实化学浓度、随机搜索、能量或最优路径。紫点与金点都是解释层。把图层藏起来不会改变模型。身体插图、巢剖面与发育记录的空间/时间尺度不同，均不作测量工具。

narration.label: 先认识这位小伙伴
narration.text: 找到蓝色标记的 W1。它头上那一对会转弯的细长结构是触角，不是腿。请从身体中间数一数，左边三条足，右边三条足，一共六条。再找找嘴边的大颚。接下来我们跟的，还是这一只工蚁。
narration.cue: 选择触角、六足与大颚，再切到出巢找食物。

narration.label: 先找到，再留下线索
narration.text: 开始时，地上还没有这次寻找食物的紫色小路。W1 一边探索，一边向前。找到食物后，它返回巢口，经过的地方才出现紫点。那是我们画出来的气味线索，不是真实的小珠子。等它回来，伙伴们才加入这一次示意招募。
narration.cue: 播放至约40%，暂停比较已标记和未标记的位置。

narration.label: 线索改变，困难也不同
narration.text: 线索变弱时，工蚁会多搜索；有过路线经验的 W1 也许能找回方向。若是一块石头堵路，闻到气味也不能穿过去。看它沿石头上方实际寻找通道，返回时才把新路逐段标出来。这是一种成功的可能，不是每次都有答案。
narration.cue: 在第三站比较减弱与阻断；查看54%、75%及95%。

narration.label: 巢里是另一段时间
narration.text: W1 把食物带回同一个巢。照料工蚁 N1 已在这里；我们另外记录的 L1 还是一粒卵。拖动它的生命记录，看幼虫、蛹和新成虫。这要比一次找食物长得多。蚁后负责产卵，不是拿着地图指挥大家的队长。
narration.cue: 进入巢内，推进觅食至终点，再独立查看L1四阶段并观察一次照料。

en.question: How does one worker sense local information, and how does a colony live together without a commander?
en.observe: Inspect W1's antennae, six legs and mandibles. Begin foraging and locate the first chemical markers. Compare a weakening cue with a physical blockage while tracking W1. Enter the same nest, then use a separate record for L1's egg, larval, pupal and adult stages.

academic.title: Anatomy connects sensing and action
academic.body: Antennae detect chemicals and contact; three leg pairs attach to the thoracic portion of the mesosoma, while mandibles are mouthparts. The waist, gaster and exoskeleton serve different functions. These drawings distinguish structures rather than identify species. Separate observed contact or turning from inferences about the information an animal used.

academic.title: Trails and experience inform local choices
academic.body: Research on Lasius niger examines chemical cues alongside route memory. Here fixed individuals mark locations only after actually returning through them. We distinguish weak signals from obstructed passage. Search paths, successful recall and the detour are finite teaching examples, not stochastic forecasts or guaranteed shortest routes.

academic.title: Development differs from colony organisation
academic.body: L1's developmental record belongs to another individual, not adult W1 turning back into a larva. Workers care for young, maintain nests and forage; queens mainly reproduce rather than issue individual commands. Local encounters, brood needs and surroundings influence activity. Tasks, nests, reproductive systems and chemical communication differ among species.

en.misconception: Hiding purple marks hides an explanatory overlay, not pheromone. A queen is not a commander, and an orderly trail is not proof of a universal shortest-path algorithm.
en.boundary: Four outdoor workers, one care worker and a queen are finite teaching characters. Paths, recruitment delay, successful memory, cue decay and detour success are authored. Chemical diffusion, wind, measured concentrations, stochastic search, energetics and optimal routing are not simulated. Purple and gold are explanatory overlays; hiding them does not change the model. Anatomy, nest cutaway and development have different illustrative space/time scales and are not measuring tools.

narration.label: Meet this worker
narration.text: Find blue-marked W1. The two elbowed structures on its head are antennae, not legs. Count three legs on each side of the middle region: six altogether. Locate the mandibles by the mouth. We will follow this same worker outside.
narration.cue: Select antennae, legs and mandibles, then open Find food.

narration.label: Discover, then mark
narration.text: At first there is no purple trail for this food. W1 searches and eventually finds it. On returning, it marks only places already passed. Purple makes an invisible chemical clue visible; real scent is not a string of beads. Nestmates then join this illustrative recruitment.
narration.cue: Play to about40%, then compare marked and unmarked ground.

narration.label: Different changes, different problems
narration.text: Weak clues can lead to more searching; experienced W1 may recover a direction. A stone is different: scent cannot let an ant walk through it. Watch W1 explore above it and mark a new path on return. This is one possible success, not a guaranteed answer.
narration.cue: Compare faster decay and blockage at the third station; inspect54%,75% and95%.

narration.label: Another timescale inside
narration.text: W1 brings food to the same nest. N1 is a different care worker, and L1 is a separate young individual. Review its egg, larval, pupal and new-adult record. Development takes far longer than a food trip. The queen lays eggs, rather than directing workers with a map.
narration.cue: Enter the nest and finish the foraging journey; independently inspect all four L1 stages and a care visit.

references.title: Czaczkes et al. — Trail pheromone and route learning in Lasius niger
Deborah Gordon — Collective wisdom of ants
